staged_source_snapshot.description: Stage 01 reproduced against this staged vulnerable checkout, and the file and line locations below are grounded in this tree. The sample metadata names vulnerable commit `c6c6a404e06ea5c6ccb5b549f498a1041b871b3f`, but the prepared workspace used for the staged reproduction is the commit above.

classification.classification_note: AddressSanitizer reports `heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 1` at `lib/Parser/JSLexer.cpp:956`. Source-grounded analysis shows the read happens because `consumeBracedCodePoint()` keeps iterating after `error()` has already forced EOF, then dereferences `curCharPtr_` one byte past the source buffer.

bug_description.original: OSS-Fuzz issue 42485232 (hermes): Heap-buffer-overflow READ 1 found by fuzz target fuzzer-jsi-entry [asan]. https://issues.oss-fuzz.com/issues/42485232
bug_description.normalized: After `JSLexer::advance()` reads the first witness byte `0x5c` and selects its backslash case, `consumeUnicodeEscape()` parses the exact prefix `\u{` and `consumeBracedCodePoint()` reads the trailing space as the first code-point payload byte. That invalid byte calls `error()`. In the saved runtime, `SimpleDiagHandlerRAII` has set the lexer error limit to 1, so `error()` forces EOF and returns false. The invalid-character arm ignores that false return, executes `failed = true; continue;`, the `for` header still increments `curCharPtr_` from `bufferEnd_` to `bufferEnd_ + 1`, and the next line-956 loop-condition read performs the observed out-of-bounds read.

source.description: First project-code statement on the crashing path that reads the fuzzed JavaScript source and dispatches on its leading byte.
source.value_from: The staged `poc` is exactly 4 bytes `5C 75 7B 20` (`\u{ `). This switch reads the first byte `0x5c` from `curCharPtr_` and selects `case '\\'`, carrying the remaining attacker-controlled prefix `u{ ` into Unicode-escape parsing.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

root_cause.description: Missing check of `error()`'s boolean return in the invalid-character arm. When the first lexer error reaches the configured error limit, `error()` forces EOF and returns false, but this caller still falls through to `failed = true; continue;` instead of aborting the braced-codepoint parse.
root_cause.note: The staged patch fixes this exact site by returning immediately when `error()` returns false, so the loop never executes the `continue;` path that lets the `for` header increment past `bufferEnd_`.

sink.description: ASan sink. The loop-condition dereference executes after the cursor has already been advanced to `bufferEnd_ + 1`, so it reads one byte past the source buffer.
sink.note: Stage 01's saved AddressSanitizer report is `heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 1` at `lib/Parser/JSLexer.cpp:956` with stack `consumeBracedCodePoint -> consumeUnicodeEscape -> advance`.

parser_admitted.description: The staged witness has already entered Hermes's JavaScript parser here; tokenization of the first source token begins when `lexer_.advance()` is called.

error_limit_configured.description: The compilation path used in the saved reproduction installs this handler, so the first lexer error in the witness reaches the error limit and `JSLexer::error()` forces EOF.

tainted_value_origin.description: The first payload byte after the function's prologue skips `{` is materialized as `ch`; for this witness it is ASCII space `0x20`, which is neither hex nor `}` and drives the invalid-character path.
tainted_value_origin.value_from: The fourth and final byte of the exact `poc` witness `5C 75 7B 20` (`\u{ `).
tainted_value_origin.note: At this point `consumeBracedCodePoint()` has already executed `++curCharPtr_` past `{`, so `curCharPtr_` is reading the witness's trailing space.

fine_trace.note: Source. `advance()` reads the witness's first byte `0x5c` from `curCharPtr_`. Because it is backslash, the switch selects `case '\\'`; the remaining attacker-controlled bytes `u{ ` stay queued for Unicode-escape parsing.
Within the selected backslash case, this call hands the same cursor to `consumeUnicodeEscape()`. At entry `curCharPtr_` still points at the leading backslash of the exact witness `\u{ `.

After step 2 consumes `\\u`, this branch reads the next byte `{` and dispatches into `consumeBracedCodePoint()`. That callee's prologue advances once more past `{`, so the only remaining payload byte before `bufferEnd_` is the trailing space and there is no closing `}`.

This statement materializes the PoC's fourth and final byte `0x20` (space) as `ch`. It is neither hex nor `}`, `curCharPtr_` is not yet `bufferEnd_`, and this is the first loop iteration so `failed` is still false; execution therefore enters the invalid-character arm and its `if (!failed && errorOnFail)` block.

The invalid-character arm calls `error()` on the space from step 4. In the saved runtime, `BCProviderFromSrc::createBCProviderFromSrc()` installs `SimpleDiagHandlerRAII`, which sets the error limit to 1, so this first lexer error reaches the limit: `forceEOF()` sets `curCharPtr_ = bufferEnd_` and `error()` returns false.

Root cause. After step 5 has already forced EOF and returned false, this caller ignores that result, executes `failed = true; continue;`, and stays in the loop instead of returning `llvm::None`. The staged patch adds the missing `if (!error(...)) { return llvh::None; }` guard at this exact site.

Because step 6 executes `continue;` without returning, the `for` header's increment `++curCharPtr_` still runs after the loop body. With `curCharPtr_` already equal to `bufferEnd_`, that increment advances it to `bufferEnd_ + 1`, past the zero terminator that `initializeWithBufferId()` requires at `*bufferEnd_`.

Sink. The next iteration reevaluates `*curCharPtr_ != '}'` with `curCharPtr_ == bufferEnd_ + 1`, so the loop condition performs the observed 1-byte out-of-bounds read. AddressSanitizer reports `heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 1` at this exact line.

allocation_context.note: ASan reports the invalid read is 0 bytes to the right of a 32-byte region allocated here by `make_unique<StringBuffer>(s)`.

format.name: raw JavaScript source
format.contract: Exactly the 4-byte witness stored in `gt_results/arvo_42485232/poc`: `5C 75 7B 20` (`\u{ `). Parsed as JavaScript source, the first token begins with a backslash, the next two bytes are `u{`, the first braced-codepoint payload byte is a space (not hex), and the file ends without any closing `}`. In the saved Stage 01 runtime, `SimpleDiagHandlerRAII` sets the lexer error limit to 1, so that first invalid-character diagnostic forces EOF; because the vulnerable code ignores the false return from `error()`, the lexer advances past `bufferEnd_` and the next line-956 loop-condition read crashes. The staged artifacts do not prove broader malformed braced escapes beyond this exact witness.
